- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending up, reduce forecasted highs by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overshoot the low — cap forecast decline at 10% below prior peak.  
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is trending down, increase forecasted lows by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days) — add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits short-term noise — apply 1–2% smoothing to forecast mean over 30-day horizon.  
- Forecast errors cluster near 10–15 day mark — adjust for mean reversion by adding 0.5–1.5% upward bias if prior 10-day average was below 30-day average.
